oewn-13954178-n.learner: being friends with someone, or being friendly with them.
examples: Between him and Darcy there was a very steady friendship, in spite of a great opposition of character.
You appear to me, Mr. Darcy, to allow nothing for the influence of friendship and affection.

oewn-00626700-a.learner: big, or fairly big, in number, amount, size, or degree.
examples: Their powers of conversation were considerable.
she had spent a considerable time in that very part of Derbyshire to which he belonged

oewn-05609513-n.learner: one of the parts that make up a person's face: the eyes, the nose, the mouth, and the chin.
examples: she had hardly a good feature in her face
A deeper shade of hauteur overspread his features, but he said not a word

oewn-05858316-n.learner: a part or quality of something that stands out.
examples: The tall windows are the best feature of the room.
Cheap tickets were a feature of the new plan.

oewn-06627379-n.learner: the main full-length film in a show at a cinema.
examples: The feature began after two short films.
We arrived late and missed the start of the feature.

oewn-01060995-v.learner: to show that you know someone or something is there, or that you know them.
examples: Could he expect to be noticed again by the regiment, after such an affront to Colonel Forster?
do not expect to be noticed by his family or friends, if you wilfully act against the inclinations of all

oewn-02122959-v.learner: to take note of something, or to become aware of it.
examples: In another minute Mr. Bingley, but without seeming to have noticed what passed, took leave and rode on with his friend.

oewn-02158938-v.learner: to find out that something is there or is so by seeing it with your eyes.
examples: Elizabeth noticed every sentence conveying the idea of uneasiness, with an attention which it had hardly received on the first perusal.

oewn-00931533-n.learner: the act of making written works.
examples: in two very short periods of writing--one of about three years, and another of not much more than five--she executed six capital works

oewn-00615511-n.learner: the work of putting something down in written words.
examples: Much as I abominate writing, I would not give up Mr. Collins's correspondence for any consideration.

oewn-06374360-n.learner: what a writer has produced, or anything set down in letters of the alphabet, thought of above all for its style and its effect.
examples: The writing in her last chapter is calm and clear.
That letter was a fine piece of writing.

oewn-09843763-n.learner: a person who knows a subject so well that people treat what they say as settled.
examples: without actually naming her authority, but stating it to be such as might be relied on
That is not very likely; our authority was too good.
when sanctioned by the express authority of both your excellent parents, my proposals will not fail of being acceptable

oewn-05203850-n.learner: the power or the right to give orders or to make decisions.
examples: Elizabeth was at no loss to understand from whence this deference for her authority proceeded

oewn-06726451-n.learner: a gentle telling-off, or a mild word of blame.
examples: no ungenerous reproach shall ever pass my lips when we are married
When she came to that part of the letter in which her family were mentioned, in tones of such mortifying, yet merited, reproach
His conduct brought reproach on the whole family.
She lived without reproach of any kind.

connotation.why: marks the thing named as a source of shame

oewn-05676878-n.learner: a settled custom that someone keeps to.
examples: Mrs. Bennet was not in the habit of walking, Mary could never spare time, but the remaining five set off together.
I would really rather not sit down before those who must be in the habit of hearing the very best performers

oewn-00415192-n.learner: a way of acting that comes by itself in a certain situation; a person may be born with it or build it up by doing it again and again.
examples: She had a habit of twisting her ring whenever she was nervous.
Blinking at a bright light is a habit of the body.

oewn-00949739-n.learner: the taking of drugs too much.
examples: He stole to pay for his habit.
She had kicked the habit after two hard years.

oewn-04937655-n.learner: one of the ways in which something shows itself.
examples: His anger took the form of a cold silence.
Help came in the form of a loan from her uncle.

oewn-05847533-n.learner: a group of things put together because they share some quality.
examples: Dancing is a form of art.
Chess and cards are two forms of game.

oewn-05071206-n.learner: any of the qualities of how something sits in space, above all the line that runs round its edge.
examples: The pond has the form of a rough circle.
He drew the form of the hill in a few strokes.

oewn-13274322-n.learner: a thing added to what you have already.
examples: I have reason to expect an addition to our family party.
the week preceding it was to bring an addition to the family at Rosings

oewn-00364614-n.learner: the act of putting one thing together with another.
examples: The addition of a fourth name to the list took only a moment.
Bread is made better by the addition of a little salt.

oewn-02682269-n.learner: a part put onto something to make it better.
examples: The new porch was a fine addition to the cottage.
A second sink was a useful addition to the kitchen.
